claim: SFO's Quiet Airport program reduced individual paging occurrences from 492 to 261 (a 47% reduction) and cumulative paging duration from 145 minutes to 58 minutes (a 60% reduction).
source_title: Inside San Francisco Airport's 'Quiet Airport' Initiative
supporting_excerpt: individual paging was reduced from 492 to 261 occurrences, with cumulative duration dropping from 145 minutes to 58 minutes — a 47% reduction in occurrences and a 60% cut to duration.
data_vintage: Post-2020 implementation of SFO Quiet Airport policy
units: paging occurrences per day; minutes per day
caveat: Trade-press reporting of airport-supplied figures; original measurement methodology not published in a primary source located for this brief.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport policy is credited with removing roughly 90 minutes of daily announcement time and achieving greater than 40 percent reduction in overall onsite noise.
supporting_excerpt: successfully removed over 90 minutes of unnecessary daily noise and achieved a reduction of more than 40 percent in overall onsite noise
caveat: Figures are as reported by SFO and its design partner; underlying acoustic measurement protocol and instrumentation not disclosed in the cited page.

claim: London City Airport has operated a 'silent terminal' policy since 2008 in which no routine tannoy announcements are made in the departure lounge; passengers rely on information screens, and announcements are reserved for bad-weather delays or genuine emergencies.
source_title: Silent Airport Policy | London City Airport
supporting_excerpt: From 2008, the airport implemented a 'silent terminal' policy... No tannoy announcements are made throughout the departure lounge... Announcements are made only for bad weather delays or genuine emergencies.
caveat: London City's passenger mix (small London-based business travellers, single terminal, no long-haul international) is unlike IAD's; policy transferability is a design question, not an assumption.

claim: Boston Medical Center reduced weekly audible cardiac alarms by 89 percent (from 62,793 to 3,970) and reduced measured noise from 90 dB pre-pilot to 72 dB after implementing a reclassification protocol that eliminated self-resetting alarms on its telemetry unit.
source_title: Hospital alleviates alarm fatigue by decreasing noise
supporting_excerpt: the largest decrease came from changes to monitors for bradycardia, tachycardia and heart rate parameter limits, which dropped from 62,793 to 3,970 weekly alarms. Noise levels fell to 72 decibels from 90 decibels pre-pilot.
units: audible cardiac alarms per week; dB (unweighted)
caveat: Non-airport precedent used for pattern-matching on policy-driven acoustic gains; dB scale (A-weighted vs. unweighted) not specified in the cited release.

claim: By January 2013 Boston Medical Center had extended its alarm-reduction protocol to 310 of 332 beds on medical/surgical units.
source_title: Boston Medical Center Tackles Alarm Fatigue and Noise
supporting_excerpt: By January 2013, 310 of 332 beds on medical/surgical units were operating under the new alarm standards and seeing significant alarm reductions.
caveat: Cited to support the pattern of pilot-to-scale within 18 months for acoustic-outcome interventions.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends maintaining a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB(A) and a minimum Speech Transmission Index of 0.45 for public-address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges to ensure clearly audible announcements.
source_title: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems (ACRP Report 175), Chapter 3 – Speech Intelligibility
supporting_excerpt: This study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges to ensure that announcements are clearly audible to passengers.
caveat: ACRP guidance is a recommended baseline; local design targets typically layer additional requirements from IEC 60268-16 and EN 54-16 for voice-alarm systems.

claim: IEC 60268 Annex G recommends STI of 0.50 as an appropriate target value for voice-address (VA) systems.
source_title: Speech Transmission Index for Public Address Systems
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268, Annex G, suggests that an STI 0.50 rating is an appropriate target value for VA (voice address) systems.
data_vintage: Reflects current IEC 60268-16 revision as of publication
denominator: Voice-address system performance at listener position
caveat: Secondary citation of the IEC standard; for regulatory or contract citation the primary reference is IEC 60268-16 (Sound system equipment – Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index), Annex G.

claim: IEC 60268-16 defines the Speech Transmission Index (STI) as the objective rating methodology for speech intelligibility of sound systems; Annex G provides recommended target values by system type.
source_title: IEC 60268-16 Sound system equipment – Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index
source_citation: International Electrotechnical Commission, IEC 60268-16 (current edition), Annex G
supporting_excerpt: Standard defines STI methodology and Annex G tabulates recommended target STI values for voice-alarm and public-address system categories.
data_vintage: Standard is periodically revised; cite current edition applicable to project.
airport_or_entity: International standard applicable to airport voice-alarm and PA design
caveat: Print-only paywalled standard; cited without URL per research contract; librarian-actionable reference.

claim: AviaVox's automated passenger-announcement platform is used by more than 130 airlines worldwide, supports over 35 languages and dialects, is CUPPS-compliant, and can operate on existing PA or PABX infrastructure including legacy systems.
source_title: For Airlines – Improve Boarding Efficiency By Up To 14% | AviaVox
supporting_excerpt: AGC's automated boarding announcements are used by over 130 airlines worldwide... deliver passenger announcements in over 35 languages and dialects... CUPPS compliant... can use your existing PA or PABX system, including legacy systems.
data_vintage: Vendor claims as of 2026 site content
caveat: Vendor self-reported install base and efficiency claims; independent third-party validation not located for this brief.

claim: The Buitenschot Land Art Park adjacent to Amsterdam Schiphol, using a landscape pattern of ridges and ditches, has approximately halved the decibel level of ground noise from Polderbaan runway operations in adjacent communities.
source_title: This Crazy Land Art Deflects Noise From Amsterdam's Airport
supporting_excerpt: Maze-like landscaping has cut the decibel level of the ambient noise at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport in half. To the southwest of the airport, there's a series of hedges and ditches laid out like interlocking diamonds as an 80-acre green space called the Buitenschot Land Art Park, whose main purpose is to deflect ground noise.
denominator: Ambient noise near Polderbaan runway approach
caveat: Cited as an unconventional-reuse precedent; measurement methodology and dB weighting not specified in the source.

claim: The DC Airports mobile app, MWAA's official app for IAD and DCA, provides push notifications to departing travelers for outbound-flight events including delays and gate changes, security wait times, and turn-by-turn wayfinding to the gate.
supporting_excerpt: Departing travelers receive push notifications for their outbound flight, such as delays and gate changes... plan and book parking in advance, check on the current security wait time, and receive turn-by-turn wayfinding guides to their gate.
airport_or_entity: Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA), IAD and DCA
caveat: Cited to establish that the redundant push-notification channel already exists; adoption rate and share of passengers with the app installed not located for this brief.

claim: MWAA has enrolled both IAD and DCA in the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower program, allowing passengers with invisible disabilities to opt into a lanyard-based recognition scheme at pre-security, baggage-claim, and USO lounge information desks at both airports.
source_title: Sunflower Hidden Disabilities Program debuts at DC's 2 airports
supporting_excerpt: Travelers can ask to join the Sunflower Hidden Disabilities program at the pre-security, baggage claims or USO lounge information desks at Washington Dulles International Airport and Ronald R. Reagan Washington National Airport.
data_vintage: Program launched at MWAA airports; date per source
caveat: Local news reporting of an MWAA program launch; primary MWAA press release not located for this brief.
